events.text: Objective: Decide whether Aquaporin should invest in a differentiated consumer proposition for one specific use case, beyond its existing water membrane offering, and identify what evidence would justify that investment. Work as an outside analyst using public sources only.. Constraints: Outside analyst using public sources only, with no contact with the company and no knowledge of its intentions; Company financial data may be incomplete, so report what could not be found; Test budget of 20000 EUR and 12-week limit are analyst assumptions, not company figures; 7 searches remain and 1 challenge is kept; Company assertions must not be presented as proof of consumer demand. Alternatives: No expansion: keep selling membranes to OEM and B2B partners only; Product redesign: build a consumer-ready purifier or cartridge on existing membrane technology; Different route to buyers: license membranes to existing consumer appliance brands rather than selling direct; Different customer group: target institutional, emergency or off-grid water users such as relief agencies and remote communities; Different use case: focus on one segment such as travel, outdoor or premium home filtration; Defer: run low-cost demand validation before committing to any product build.
Searched for "Aquaporin consumer water filter product"; found aqp-dwd-recital40-confidence, aqp-flanders-bottled-perceptions, aqp-flint-filters-not-working.
Searched for "Aquaporin Inside membrane partner purifier"; found aqp-philips-china-supply-2023, aqp-vestel-rafine-pro-2024, aqp-strategic-review-failed.

T1: Households buy point-of-use purifiers when they distrust tap water, so a membrane that is visibly certified for removing contaminants can command a price premium, but only if an appliance brand carries it to market. Who benefits: Household drinking-water buyers who distrust tap water, and the appliance brand that sells the purifier; the membrane supplier gains through a per-unit component royalty or supply margin.. Why behaviour changes: Negative perception of tap water (safety, taste) drives purchase, as seen in Flanders where many consumers see tap water as unsafe and prefer bottled. A purifier answers that perception, and the certification and brand signal the safety claim.. How value is captured: Aquaporin licenses or supplies its membrane to an appliance maker such as Vestel, which sells the purifier under its own brand. Aquaporin earns per-unit component revenue, not retail margin.. Assumptions: Tap water distrust is widespread enough in the target market to create purchase intent; Consumers pay for the purifier mainly because of the trust signal, not membrane performance details; The appliance partner has retail reach and sells the unit at a price that leaves room for a component margin; The membrane's performance advantage is verifiable and communicable. Predictions: Purchase rates for purifiers rise in markets with higher reported tap water distrust; Partner sell-through depends more on brand and retail placement than on the membrane's technical specification; Component margin per unit stays small relative to the partner's retail price.

T2: Consumers buy filtration mainly as a one-off or replaceable habit tied to cartridge replacement and maintenance, so value depends on recurring consumable sales rather than the membrane unit price; a membrane supplier only captures this if it controls the cartridge. Who benefits: Households who want low-effort filtration, and the party that supplies replacement cartridges; the membrane supplier benefits only if its membrane is the consumable.. Why behaviour changes: Flint's experience shows filters often are not used or maintained correctly (50 to 70 percent not working in one clinic estimate), so the value of a purifier depends on sustained correct use, which a consumable model can secure and a one-time sale cannot.. How value is captured: Aquaporin would capture recurring revenue by making its membrane the replaceable cartridge or by licensing it to a partner whose cartridge is sold on subscription, rather than earning a single component fee per appliance.. Assumptions: Consumers keep buying replacement cartridges if the product is easy to maintain and the performance is visible; The membrane can be packaged as a cartridge without losing performance or raising cost beyond what consumers accept; Partners will share cartridge revenue or allow the membrane to be the consumable. Predictions: Repeat cartridge purchase rates fall sharply when maintenance is complicated or unclear; Products with auto-reminders or subscription delivery show higher sustained use than those without; Revenue per household is driven more by consumable frequency than by the initial appliance sale.

T1 supports, from aqp-flanders-bottled-perceptions (independent_study): "For a large part, this is caused by negative perceptions about tap water. Many consumers consider it unhealthy, unsafe and prefer the taste of bottled water.". Does not show: It is a bottled-water study from Flanders, abstract only. It does not measure purifier purchase, willingness to pay for a membrane, or any appliance-brand sales. It cannot show that a trust signal drives purifier purchase, or that the partner captures a viable margin..

T2 supports, from aqp-flint-filters-not-working (customer_observation): "“Anywhere from 50 to 70 percent of folks that we’re seeing have filters that are not working,” Hood says, adding that it’s irresponsible to tell people it’s safe to drink filtered water when so many people aren’t using filters correctly.". Does not show: This is one official's estimate about one city's filters in 2016, with no sample or method. It does not show that maintenance drives repeat cartridge purchases, nor how often consumers replace cartridges, nor that a membrane supplier could capture that revenue..
Looked for evidence against T1: "Aquaporin consumer purifier sales revenue partner low volume withdrawal"; found aqp-philips-china-supply-2023, aqp-strategic-review-failed, aqp-coway-rental-growth.

Declined to test: Aquaporin announced withdrawal of its offering and insolvency proceedings on 30 January 2026, after failing to find funding or partners. A 20000 EUR, 12-week consumer test cannot fix that financing gap, and it would only inform a buyer of the assets. The partner model has company-claimed traction (Vestel, Philips China) but no sales figures were found. More testing is not worth its cost before the insolvency outcome is known.

Favours T1: Do not invest in a Aquaporin-led consumer proposition. The company has announced withdrawal of its offering and insolvency proceedings (30 January 2026), so the question is not whether to develop a consumer product but whether any buyer of its assets could run a partner-led purifier model. If an acquirer appears, the partner (B2B2C) route is the only one with observed traction, and it should be validated with partner sell-through data before any capital is committed. No test is recommended at this stage. Beliefs: T1: uncertain; T2: uncertain.

Recommendation: Do not invest in a consumer proposition led by Aquaporin. Its own announcement of 30 January 2026 says it withdrew its offering and resolved to start insolvency proceedings after failing to find funding or partners. The live question is whether a buyer of its assets could run the partner-led purifier model, which is the only route with observed consumer traction. No test is recommended before the insolvency outcome is known. Target customer: Household drinking-water buyers who distrust tap water, reached through an appliance brand's retail channel (for example Vestel in Turkey, or Philips-branded purifiers in China). Not a direct-to-consumer customer for Aquaporin.. Value proposition: For a partner appliance brand: a certified membrane sold as a component inside its own purifier, giving a trust signal on contaminant removal. For Aquaporin or an acquirer: component supply and licence revenue, not retail margin. Unproven for the household.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Monitor the insolvency proceedings and any asset sale. If a buyer emerges, request partner sell-through figures and supply volumes from Vestel and AquaShield/Philips, since the company announcements give no unit or revenue data for the consumer line. Only then consider a validation test.. Uncertainty: Aquaporin's financial statements, consumer-line revenue, partner volumes and unit prices were not found in public sources, so the commercial size of the partner route is unknown. The partner announcements (Vestel 2024, Philips China 2023) are company claims with no sales figures. The Flanders evidence is an abstract on bottled water, and the Flint estimate is one official's figure from 2016. The T2 cartridge-maintenance theory has no direct evidence of Aquaporin consumable revenue.. Would change if: A buyer acquires the membrane and partner contracts and publishes sell-through or supply volumes showing recurring demand; Vestel or AquaShield/Philips reports purifier sales or repeat cartridge purchases, which would support T1 and T2 respectively; Evidence that the partner margin on each unit is material to the partner, which would strengthen T1; Evidence that consumers replace or keep using cartridges at high rates, which would favour the consumable model over a one-off component sale; Confirmation that insolvency proceedings end the consumer line entirely, which would close the question. Beliefs: T1: uncertain; T2: uncertain.

case.question: Should RATIONAL develop a differentiated proposition for home cooks, building on its commercial combi-steamer technology, or stay with professional kitchens? What evidence would justify either choice?
case.source_limits: Evidence is limited to the case dossier: each source shows everything the dossier holds for it, often a short excerpt, not the whole original. Results marked simulated are what-if evidence, not real observations.

sources.excerpt: In addition to the professional food-service models, there are also smaller combi steamers for private household use.
Germany: RATIONAL AG , Gaggenau Hausgeräte , PALUX, Convotherm, MKN, ELOMA, Miele , AEG (part of Electrolux), Bosch.
According to company estimates, the global market potential for combi-steamers is 4.8 million customers, around 75% of whom still use traditional cooking appliances.
From 1978 onwards, the company concentrated solely on combi steamers and discontinued all other product lines.

events.text: Objective: Decide whether RATIONAL AG should build a differentiated proposition for home cooks using its commercial combi-steamer technology, or keep its focus on professional kitchens. Identify what evidence would justify either choice, and verify what the company already does with individual buyers.. Constraints: Outside analyst working only from public sources; no contact with the company and no knowledge of its intentions; Financial data is partly public; gaps and reconciliation problems must be stated, not filled in; Test budget of EUR 20,000 and a 12-week limit are analyst assumptions, not company figures; Search budget is 8 searches, 7 remaining; read sources before theorising; Any claim about current consumer sales must be traced to a source I have read; Company statements about its own plans are not evidence of demand. Alternatives: No expansion: stay with professional kitchens and keep the current product line and channel; Consumer-grade redesign: a smaller, lower-cost or simplified combi-steamer aimed at home cooks; Same product, different route: sell or license existing units to home buyers through retail or a partner, without redesign; Different customer group: premium home enthusiasts or small food businesses (bakeries, caterers) rather than mainstream home cooks; Adjacent category: software, recipes or cooking-guidance services using the steaming know-how, without a hardware push into homes; Licensing or component supply of the steaming technology to appliance makers who already reach home buyers.
Searched for "RATIONAL combi steamer home consumer"; found rational-combi-makers, rational-ir-potential, rational-wiki-1978.

T1: Home cooks will pay a premium for a compact, consumer-priced combi-steamer that brings professional steaming results to the home, so RATIONAL could earn margin by reusing its core technology in a home-sized, branded product. Who benefits: RATIONAL AG (new margin and unit volume) and home cooks seeking healthier, faster cooking. Why behaviour changes: Home cooks who already value health and cooking quality treat steaming as a desirable way to cook; a credible professional brand and a size that fits a home kitchen reduce the perceived gap between a home appliance and a restaurant-grade tool.. How value is captured: Premium retail price on a branded product, sold direct or through appliance retail, with margin from the same engineering base. Assumptions: A meaningful share of home cooks would pay a premium over conventional ovens for steaming; Kitchen space, installation and price do not block purchase at scale; RATIONAL can design a home unit without a prohibitive cost increase. Predictions: Stated willingness to pay for a home unit at a premium price exceeds the unit cost by a margin that supports the business case; Conversion from interest to purchase is higher among owners of compact or built-in kitchens than among owners of standard kitchens; Sales hold after the novelty phase, measured by repeat use and second-order purchases.

T2: Home cooks will not buy a combi-steamer in meaningful numbers because space, installation and the habit of using the existing oven limit demand, so the professional channel remains the only place where RATIONAL's technology captures value. Who benefits: RATIONAL AG and its professional dealer and service network, which already capture value from commercial kitchens. Why behaviour changes: Home cooks rarely replace a working oven; a combi-steamer needs counter or built-in space, a power supply and a reason to change routine. Without a strong reason the behaviour does not change, so demand stays small.. How value is captured: Continued sales of professional units, service contracts and consumables to commercial kitchens, which carry higher unit prices and recurring revenue. Assumptions: Home buyers view steaming as an occasional feature, not a replacement for the main oven; Installation and space needs are a binding constraint for most households; Professional kitchens remain a larger and more profitable market than home kitchens. Predictions: Home interest measured in a survey is high but purchase intent falls sharply once price and space are stated; Households with a recent kitchen refit show higher purchase intent than those without; Recurring revenue per commercial customer remains higher than any plausible home revenue per household.

T1 neutral, from rational-ir-potential (company_assertion): "According to company estimates, the global market potential for combi-steamers is 4.8 million customers, around 75% of whom still use traditional cooking appliances.". Does not show: It does not say whether the 4.8 million customers are home cooks or professional kitchens, does not give willingness to pay, and is a company estimate with no stated method. It cannot show a premium home product would sell..

T2 neutral, from rational-combi-makers (market_fact): "Germany: RATIONAL AG , Gaggenau Hausgeräte , PALUX, Convotherm, MKN, ELOMA, Miele , AEG (part of Electrolux), Bosch.". Does not show: The excerpt is a bare list of names under a Germany heading. It does not say which of these sell combi-steamers to households, at what volume, or whether the home units are the same technology. It neither confirms nor rules out T2's claim that home demand is small..
Looked for evidence against T2: "home consumers buy combi steamer household demand"; found rational-combi-countertop, rational-combi-history, rational-combi-household.

T2 contradicts, from rational-combi-household (market_fact): "In addition to the professional food-service models, there are also smaller combi steamers for private household use.". Does not show: It shows that household combi steamers exist, not that they sell in volume, earn margin, or are made by RATIONAL. The excerpt is a general Wikipedia statement with no figures. It weakens T2's premise that home products are not on offer, but not its claim that the professional channel captures more value..

Test "Priced pre-order test for a compact home combi-steamer, Germany" between T1; T2. Method: Run a bilingual landing page offering a refundable EUR 100 deposit toward a compact home unit, with two randomised price frames (EUR 1,490 and EUR 1,890, proposed) and a stated space and installation requirement shown on half the traffic. Drive paid and panel traffic to the page. Track deposits, not stated interest.. Sample: About 6,000 qualified visitors (proposed) drawn from German home-cooking audiences, split across four arms; a second cell of around 400 panel respondents who own compact or built-in kitchens (proposed) for a survey of purchase intent with space shown.. Measure: Deposit conversion rate per 1,000 unique visitors, by price frame and by space-disclosure frame; drop-off at the space and installation step.. Predictions: T1: Deposit conversion stays at or above threshold at the higher price, and the gap between space-disclosed and space-hidden arms is small, because the premium is not blocked by kitchen fit.; T2: Deposit conversion falls below threshold at the higher price, and disclosing space and installation cuts conversion sharply, because kitchen fit and installation block purchase.. Decision rule: Proceed to a prototype-level business case only if deposit conversion is at least 1.5 per 1,000 visitors (proposed threshold, to be set against unit margin) at the EUR 1,490 price with space disclosed, and the space-disclosed arm loses no more than 30% of conversion versus the space-hidden arm (proposed). If either fails, treat T2 as the working theory and keep the professional focus.. Cost: 18500 euros, 10 weeks.

Favours T2: Do not commit to a home-cook expansion yet. Keep the professional focus as the base case, and run the priced pre-order test (X1) before any product work. Treat the home segment as an option to be tested, not a plan. Beliefs: T1: uncertain; T2: likely.

Recommendation: Keep the professional focus as the base case. Do not commit to a home-cook product now. Test home demand first with a priced, space-disclosed pre-order experiment (X1, proposed EUR 18,500, 10 weeks), and proceed only if it clears the stated threshold. Target customer: No home target chosen yet. Professional commercial kitchens remain the base. Compact-kitchen home cooks are the candidate segment to test.. Value proposition: Not yet defined for homes. The professional proposition stays as it is. A home unit would need to show it can hold a price premium despite space and installation limits.. Favoured theory: T2. Next action: Run test X1 with a refundable deposit, two price frames and a space-disclosure split. First confirm RATIONAL's consumer offering and its revenue split by channel from financial statements, which I have not read.. Uncertainty: High. Three sources read. Only one company figure: a 4.8 million customer estimate with no method and no home/professional split. A Wikipedia list names Gaggenau, Miele, AEG and Bosch as German combi-steamer makers, and another says household combi-steamers exist, but neither shows volumes, margins or whether RATIONAL sells to homes. No financial statements read. Test costs and thresholds are my proposals. T2 belief is a judgment from thin evidence.. Would change if: X1 shows deposit conversion at or above threshold at the higher price with space disclosed; Verified figures show RATIONAL already sells home units at meaningful volume; Credible evidence of strong home sales growth with professional-level margins; Financials show professional growth slowing sharply; Evidence that appliance makers dominate household steaming, favouring licensing. Beliefs: T1: uncertain; T2: likely.

case.question: Should Simonelli Group develop a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case, beyond its existing professional espresso-equipment offering? What evidence would justify that investment?
case.source_limits: Evidence is limited to the case dossier: each source shows everything the dossier holds for it, often a short excerpt, not the whole original. Results marked simulated are what-if evidence, not real observations.

sources.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. In this simulated warehouse test, a new label printer reduced packing errors slightly. Nothing about wearers or buyers was measured.
Australia’s Breville Group has announced plans to acquire Italian prosumer espresso equipment company Lelit in a deal worth €113 million ($124 million USD) in cash and shares.

Italian commercial espresso equipment manufacturer Nuova Simonelli has unveiled the Oscar Mood, a colorful new model in its most affordable machine line for homes, offices and other lower-volume environments. The Oscar Mood is the successor in the line to the Oscar II, and the original Nuova Simonelli Oscar, which introduced some of Nuova Simonelli’s high-quality and high-powered components to high-end home and prosumer audiences.

At the same time, the professional division maintained excellent momentum throughout the year, achieving revenue growth of over 40% in the fourth quarter. Both brands, La Marzocco and Eversys, delivered outstanding results, driven by the consolidated leadership of our products in the premium segments, the ability to intercept emerging trends in specialty coffee, and the rapid expansion into the prosumer market.

Obiettivo 2022 è rinnovare la linea White Eagle della Victoria ed estendere la gamma del Mythos con una versione entry level. Sempre per Victoria Arduino si prevede il lancio di un nuovo macinacaffè compatto capace di soddisfare le esigenze del caffè filtro e dell’espresso.

events.text: Objective: Decide whether Simonelli Group should invest in a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case, beyond its professional espresso-equipment business, and identify what public evidence would justify that investment. The objective is to learn whether a consumer proposition can earn a return the company cannot get from its current channels, not to choose a product design.. Constraints: Outside analyst using public sources only; the company has not asked this question and nothing here describes its intentions.; Company financial data may not be fully public; unknown figures must be reported as unknown.; Test budget 20,000 EUR and 12-week limit are analyst assumptions, not company figures.; 8 searches in total, 7 remaining; a single challenge_theory search is kept for falsification.; Simonelli's existing consumer reach is unknown and must be established from evidence before any theory relies on it.; Brands in scope: Nuova Simonelli and Victoria Arduino (commercial espresso machines and grinders).. Alternatives: A. No expansion: keep the professional focus and spend nothing on consumer development.; B. Product redesign: a smaller, simpler home-use espresso machine or grinder under an existing brand.; C. Different route to buyers: direct-to-consumer or online retail, or subscription for consumables and service on existing equipment, without a new product.; D. Different customer group: serve prosumer home baristas or small offices with a configured professional-grade machine, or a component and licensing model (grinders, boilers, brand licence) to home-appliance makers.; E. Service and parts model for the installed base: aftermarket maintenance, training or recurring revenue from existing commercial customers.; F. Staged entry: test a small consumer offer (e.g. a grinder-only or pre-order pilot) before committing to a full product line..
Searched for "Simonelli Group consumer home espresso machine grinder"; found simo-dcn-oscar-mood-2021, simo-dcn-breville-lelit-2022, simo-report2021-product-plan.

T1: Simonelli can capture value in the prosumer home segment by offering a scaled-down machine that carries its professional components and brand credibility, because enthusiast buyers pay a premium for commercial-grade parts. Who benefits: Home enthusiasts and prosumers who want commercial-grade components at home; Nuova Simonelli, which sells the premium through its existing brand and parts supply.. Why behaviour changes: Buyers who already value espresso quality want durable, high-powered components they associate with professional cafés, so a brand carrying that credibility into a smaller form factor wins their purchase over generic home machines.. How value is captured: Margin on a branded machine sold through the existing dealer and online network, plus shared component and parts volume with the commercial line, so the same engineering spend serves two segments.. Assumptions: Enthusiast buyers will pay a premium for professional-grade components in a home-sized machine.; Simonelli's existing brand and dealer network can reach these buyers without a new consumer channel.; Scaling the design down does not raise unit cost enough to erase the premium.; Professional and home lines do not cannibalise each other's sales.. Predictions: Sales of the Oscar-type home line grow faster than the commercial line in the same markets after launch.; Buyers in consumer reviews cite component quality or brand as a top purchase reason, more than price.; Dealer or online sell-through of the home model is repeat-purchase driven within 12 months.; A grinder-only or pre-order pilot converts at a rate that covers its unit cost and marketing within the test window..

T2: The prosumer home espresso segment is won by whoever controls retail reach, marketing and the consumer brand, so a commercial maker that only supplies components or a branded machine captures little of the value and should license or supply components rather than build a consumer channel. Who benefits: Consumer brands and retailers that own customer relationships and distribution (for example, the acquirer of a prosumer maker); Simonelli only if it supplies components or licenses its name.. Why behaviour changes: Home buyers choose by brand familiarity, reviews, retail presence and price promotions rather than by the professional pedigree of parts, so the owner of those levers sets the price and takes the margin.. How value is captured: Component supply, boiler or group-head sales or a licence fee to a consumer brand, with no marketing or retail cost borne by Simonelli.. Assumptions: Home espresso buyers are reached mainly through retail and consumer marketing rather than commercial-brand pedigree.; Consolidation in prosumer makers (such as a large consumer brand buying a prosumer maker) reflects where value sits.; Simonelli can supply components to consumer brands without damaging its own commercial brand.. Predictions: Consumer brands that own retail and marketing hold most prosumer espresso sales; professional-only brands have small shares.; Prosumer makers that sell direct without a retail partner grow more slowly than those with retail partners.; A component-supply or licence deal yields a fee stream with little working capital and no consumer channel cost.; Consumer purchase decisions cite brand or price over component pedigree in reviews or surveys..

T1 supports, from simo-dcn-oscar-mood-2021 (company_assertion): "The Oscar Mood is the successor in the line to the Oscar II, and the original Nuova Simonelli Oscar, which introduced some of Nuova Simonelli’s high-quality and high-powered components to high-end home and prosumer audiences.". Does not show: Sales volumes, margins, customer reasons for buying, or whether the home line grows faster than the commercial line. The 'high-quality' framing is the company's own positioning, relayed by a trade press article..

T2 supports, from simo-dcn-breville-lelit-2022 (market_fact): "has announced plans to acquire Italian prosumer espresso equipment company Lelit". Does not show: Why Breville paid this price, whether Lelit's value came from retail reach rather than product quality, or how much prosumer sales each brand controls. A deal announcement shows that a consumer-brand owner valued a prosumer maker, not the mechanism behind it. The article also contains unrelated spam links, so only the body excerpt is reliable..

Looked for evidence against T1: "home espresso buyers choose by price, retail availability and consumer brand rather than professional component pedigree"; found simo-ns-oscar-mood-page, simo-dcn-oscar-mood-2021, simo-delonghi-prosumer-2025.

T1 supports, from simo-delonghi-prosumer-2025 (company_assertion): "the rapid expansion into the prosumer market". Does not show: How much of the professional division's growth came from prosumer sales, whether those buyers chose the brand for its professional components, or whether prosumer margins are above commercial ones. The source is a company revenue release, a rival's self-report, and it does not isolate the prosumer effect. It also does not show that buyers ignore retail reach, so my challenge search found no direct contradiction of T1..

Test "Pedigree versus channel pre-order pilot for a home grinder or entry machine" between T1; T2. Method: Two-by-two online pre-order test in two EU markets. Arm 1 messaging stresses professional components and the Nuova Simonelli or Victoria Arduino pedigree. Arm 2 messaging stresses price and convenience with no pedigree claim. Half of each message is offered direct-to-consumer, half through one retail partner's listing. Visitors are shown the product and can place a refundable deposit. Product is a grinder-only or entry-level machine, a proxy that avoids a full product launch.. Sample: Proposed: about 6,000 to 8,000 qualified home-espresso visitors, drawn from paid search and social ads targeting home espresso interest, across the four cells. The sample size is an estimate chosen to detect a conversion difference of about 1.5 times with reasonable power.. Measure: Deposit conversion rate per 1,000 unique visitors by cell, and deposit value per visitor. Secondary: click-through on the pedigree claim and refund rate at week 12.. Predictions: T1: The pedigree message converts clearly better than the price message in the direct channel, because buyers pay for professional components. The retail listing adds little to conversion once pedigree is shown.; T2: Channel and brand reach drive conversion more than the pedigree claim. The retail-listed arm converts better than direct, and pedigree shows little or no advantage over price messaging.. Decision rule: Proposed threshold: favour T1 if pedigree-message deposit conversion is at least 1.5 times the price-message conversion in the direct channel, with the 95% interval excluding 1, and deposits cover at least 30% of the estimated unit margin needed. Favour T2 if the retail-listed arm converts at least 1.5 times direct and pedigree shows no advantage. Otherwise, keep both theories and do not invest.. Cost: 20000 euros, 12 weeks.

Favours T1: Do not commit to a full consumer product line yet. Run the proposed pre-order pilot (X1, 20,000 EUR, 12 weeks, estimated) to test whether the professional-component pedigree sells a home product better than a price message, and whether retail reach matters. Keep the professional business as the base. Consider a component or licence route (T2) if the pilot shows that channel and brand reach carry the sale. Beliefs: T1: uncertain; T2: uncertain.

T1 kept: SYN-D is a simulated warehouse test about a label printer. It measured nothing about wearers or buyers, so even if it were real it would bear on neither T1 nor T2, and it changes nothing. I am not citing it. T1 is kept on the real evidence already assessed: the Oscar Mood trade article and the De'Longhi release support the pedigree strategy in direction only, with no demand data. New claim: none. Evidence: simo-dcn-oscar-mood-2021; simo-delonghi-prosumer-2025.

T2 kept: Supposing SYN-D were real: it is a warehouse test of a label printer's effect on packing errors. It measured nothing about buyers, channels or brand reach, so it does not bear on whether retail reach or brand control captures value in home espresso. It changes nothing for T2. It is simulated and is not cited as evidence for any theory. New claim: none. Evidence: SYN-D.

Recommendation: Do not commit to a full consumer product line now. Keep the professional business as the base. Run a small, reversible pre-order pilot first (proposed 20,000 EUR, 12 weeks, estimated) to test whether the professional-component pedigree sells a home product better than a price message, and whether retail reach changes the answer. Fall back to a component or licence route if channel and brand reach carry the sale. Public evidence does not establish consumer demand, margins or Simonelli's consumer sales, so no investment case is justified yet. Target customer: Home espresso enthusiasts and prosumers who already value commercial-grade components. This is a hypothesis to test, not an established segment. Simonelli's actual consumer reach is unknown from public sources.. Value proposition: A smaller home machine or grinder with professional-grade components and the Nuova Simonelli or Victoria Arduino pedigree, sold at a premium over generic home equipment. Unproven: no price, margin or buyer reason has been observed.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run the pedigree-versus-channel pre-order pilot (X1) in two EU markets with the decision rule as written: favour T1 if pedigree-message deposit conversion is at least 1.5 times the price-message conversion in the direct channel, with the 95% interval excluding 1. Ask Simonelli, through a proper channel, for consumer sales, retail arrangements and prosumer margins.. Uncertainty: High. Oscar Mood (2021) shows a home-oriented launch, described by trade press from company positioning. The 2021 report plans an entry-level Mythos and compact grinder (company claim, Italian, not assessed). No public sales, margins or cannibalisation data. Breville's Lelit deal shows value to a consumer-brand owner, not why. The De'Longhi release is self-reported. One challenge search found no direct contradiction of T1. Financials not found; test figures are my estimates. SYN-D (simulated) was not used.. Would change if: Retail-listed arm converts at least 1.5 times direct and pedigree adds no lift over price, favouring T2 and a licence route.; Simonelli's data show small consumer sales or thin margins after channel costs.; Evidence that prosumer buyers choose mainly on price or retail availability, not component pedigree.; Pilot deposit conversion clears the margin threshold at a price covering unit cost.; Evidence a home line would cannibalise commercial sales.. Beliefs: T1: uncertain; T2: uncertain.

case.question: Should Aquaporin A/S develop a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case, beyond its existing water-membrane offering? What evidence would justify that investment?
case.source_limits: Evidence is limited to the case dossier: each source shows everything the dossier holds for it, often a short excerpt, not the whole original. Results marked simulated are what-if evidence, not real observations.

sources.excerpt: With only two cartridges and a replacement indicator on the machine, ONE is easy to install and use. The user friendliness continues, as ONE’s only maintenance requirement is cartridge replacement which can easily be done by oneself.

Signed an exclusive supply agreement with AquaShield, the global brand partner of Philips Water Solutions for supply of membrane to all Philips-branded purifiers in China, with a doubling of sales compared to 2022

Despite significant efforts through a period of time and as part of its strategic review in the second half of 2025, where multiple routes have been explored with the view to raise capital, enter into a strategic transaction, or a sale of part of or all of the Company's asset, the Company has not been successful in identifying investors or partners that can provide sufficient funding to continue the Company's commercialization and advancing its proprietary water technology platform. The Board of Directors does therefore not see a viable path forward to secure a sustainable financing solution as a going concern.

Turkey's leading technology company, Vestel, has launched a water purifier named Vestel Rafine PRO in cooperation with Aquaporin on its website and in selected stores across Turkey. The Aquaporin Inside® technology powers the Vestel Rafine PRO water purifier.

events.text: Objective: Decide whether Aquaporin A/S should invest in a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific use case beyond its existing water-membrane offering, and identify what public evidence would justify that investment.. Constraints: Outside analyst using public sources only, with no contact with the company and no knowledge of its intentions; Company financial data may be incomplete, so gaps must be reported; Test budget of 20000 EUR and 12-week limit are analyst assumptions, not company figures; Search budget is limited to 7 remaining searches, read and challenge steps included; Must establish what the company already sells to individual buyers before assuming; Company claims are assertions, not proof of demand. Alternatives: No expansion: remain a B2B membrane supplier with no consumer proposition; Product redesign: build a consumer-ready home drinking-water purifier or cartridge around existing membranes; Different route to buyers: supply membranes to existing consumer purifier brands as an ingredient supplier; Different customer group: target institutional or commercial buyers such as cafes, offices or hotels with a use-case unit; Use-case pivot: focus on a niche need such as travel, emergency or off-grid water; Staged option: low-cost validation through desk research or a partner pilot before any build.
Searched for "Aquaporin consumer water purifier"; found aqp-one-purifier-2021, aqp-philips-china-supply-2023, aqp-vestel-rafine-pro-2024.

T1: Individual buyers choose a home water purifier partly because it carries a recognisable, trusted membrane technology name. A membrane maker that licenses that name to established appliance brands captures a per-unit royalty or supply margin without carrying brand, retail or service costs. Who benefits: Aquaporin (ingredient-brand royalty or exclusive membrane supply) and the appliance brand partner (differentiation on a named technology).. Why behaviour changes: Buyers who cannot judge membrane performance rely on a visible technology mark and on the trust of a known appliance brand, so the named membrane shifts choice at the shelf or website.. How value is captured: Per-unit membrane supply or royalty under exclusive agreements, such as the Philips China supply and the Vestel Rafine PRO launch, with replacement cartridges as recurring volume.. Assumptions: Buyers recognise and value the Aquaporin Inside mark when it appears on a product; Partner brands pay enough per unit to cover membrane cost plus a margin; Exclusive supply limits how many rivals can use the same membrane. Predictions: Sales of partner-branded units grow faster in markets where the Aquaporin mark is displayed than where it is not; Partners renew or extend supply agreements after the first term; Partner retail listings or reviews mention the technology name as a purchase reason in a measurable share of cases.

T2: Individual buyers choose a home water purifier mainly on convenience, meaning simple installation and low-effort cartridge replacement. A company that sells its own branded unit and a recurring cartridge sets the maintenance experience and keeps cartridge revenue. Who benefits: Aquaporin, if it sells its own branded unit and recurring cartridges directly or through distributors, and the buyer, who avoids maintenance effort.. Why behaviour changes: Buyers avoid products that need technician visits or complicated filter changes, so a unit that the owner can maintain in minutes wins repeat purchase and recommendation.. How value is captured: Recurring cartridge sales over the product life, with unit margin on the device, sold through distributors that already carry the ONE purifier.. Assumptions: Installation and maintenance effort is a major reason for abandoning or not buying home purifiers; Cartridge replacement intervals create repeat revenue large enough to justify owning the consumer relationship; Distributor reach in the target markets is adequate without a direct retail build. Predictions: Owners of units with simple cartridge replacement reorder cartridges at a higher rate than owners of units needing more complex service; Reviews and returns of consumer purifiers cite installation or maintenance effort as a leading complaint; Buyers in markets with distributor coverage buy the unit at a rate that depends on local installation support.

T1 supports, from aqp-vestel-rafine-pro-2024 (company_assertion): "The Aquaporin Inside® technology powers the Vestel Rafine PRO water purifier.". Does not show: Whether buyers choose the Vestel unit because of the Aquaporin Inside mark, what share of the price the membrane earns, or whether the arrangement is exclusive or renewed. The source is the company's own press release..

T2 supports, from aqp-one-purifier-2021 (company_assertion): "ONE’s only maintenance requirement is cartridge replacement which can easily be done by oneself.". Does not show: That convenience drives purchase or repeat cartridge orders, or that buyers rank maintenance above price, performance or brand. It also gives no cartridge price, replacement interval or reorder rate. The source is the company's own product claim, not a customer observation..

Looked for evidence against T1: "technology ingredient brand does not drive consumer purchase of water purifier; partner brand sales lower or membrane commodity"; found aqp-philips-china-supply-2023, aqp-strategic-review-failed, aqp-vestel-rafine-pro-2024.
Searched for "Aquaporin insolvency asset sale buyer membrane technology"; found aqp-strategic-review-failed, aqp-philips-china-supply-2023, aqp-insolvency-2026.

Declined to test: Aquaporin announced on 30 January 2026 that it had withdrawn its offering and resolved to start insolvency proceedings, after finding no investors or partners to fund commercialisation as a going concern. A 20000 EUR consumer test cannot show whether the company should invest, because it cannot fund a build. A test could only help a possible buyer of the IP or assets, and I found no evidence of one. Any demand test would also rest on company product claims. Spending the budget would not change the decision.

Favours T1: Do not invest in a differentiated consumer proposition now. Aquaporin has announced withdrawal of its offering and insolvency proceedings (30 January 2026). Its only consumer-facing evidence is partner-led: the Vestel Rafine PRO using Aquaporin Inside, and the Philips China membrane supply. Any value from T1 would have to be captured by a buyer of the IP or by partners, not by Aquaporin funding a new build. Beliefs: T1: uncertain; T2: uncertain.

Recommendation: Do not invest in a differentiated consumer proposition for Aquaporin A/S now. The company announced on 30 January 2026 that it had withdrawn its offering and resolved to start insolvency proceedings, after finding no investors or partners to fund commercialisation as a going concern. Its public consumer footprint is partner-led (Vestel Rafine PRO using Aquaporin Inside; Philips-branded China membrane supply; the ONE purifier sold through distributors). Any value in the proposition would accrue to a buyer of the IP or assets, or to existing partners, not to a funded Aquaporin build. Target customer: No target customer is recommended for Aquaporin itself. If a buyer of the IP emerged, the only evidenced route is B2B2C supply to appliance brands, not direct sales to individual buyers.. Value proposition: Not applicable for Aquaporin's own investment. The evidenced proposition is a named membrane technology supplied to appliance partners (Aquaporin Inside), with replacement cartridges as potential recurring volume. Neither has buyer-side evidence yet.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Treat the question as a going-concern and asset-sale question, not a product question. Search for any announced buyer, asset sale or licensing of the membrane platform and of partner agreements (Philips/AquaShield, Vestel) under the insolvency process. If none appears, no consumer investment case exists.. Uncertainty: Key gaps: I found no insolvency administrator filing, no financial statements, no revenue or unit data beyond company press releases, no cartridge pricing or reorder data, and no independent buyer research. All consumer-side evidence is company assertion. I could not confirm the current status of partner agreements. The insolvency record is a third-party copy of the company announcement, and I did not verify it against a registry.. Would change if: A buyer or investor publicly acquires the membrane platform or the Philips and Vestel supply agreements and commits funding; The insolvency process is halted or a going-concern financing is announced; Independent sales data shows buyers paying a premium for the Aquaporin Inside mark, or repeat cartridge purchases at scale; Partners confirm continued supply volumes after the insolvency announcement. Beliefs: T1: uncertain; T2: uncertain.

events.text: Objective: Determine whether Simonelli Group should invest in a differentiated consumer proposition for a specific home-use case beyond its professional espresso-equipment offering, and what evidence would justify that investment.. Constraints: Outside analyst working only from public sources; the company has not asked and nothing here describes its intentions; Financial data may not be fully public; state what could not be found; Test budget of 20000 EUR and 12-week maximum are analyst assumptions, not company figures; 8 searches total, 7 remaining; first establish how far the company already reaches individual buyers; SIMULATED results cannot be cited as evidence. Alternatives: No expansion: remain professional-only and focus on existing commercial customers; Product redesign: adapt an existing commercial grinder or machine into a smaller, lower-cost home model under existing brands; Different route to buyers: sell prosumer or home models through online or retail channels, or via white-label partnerships with home-appliance brands; Different customer group: target prosumer enthusiasts or small offices rather than full commercial operators; Component supply or licensing: supply grinders or boilers to home-machine makers without a consumer brand; Acquire an existing home-espresso brand to gain consumer channel access.
Searched for "Simonelli Group home espresso consumer machines"; found simo-dcn-oscar-mood-2021, simo-dcn-breville-lelit-2022, simo-report2021-product-plan.

T1: Enthusiasts buy home espresso machines as a performance and status purchase, so a compact machine carrying commercial-grade components (as the Oscar line already does) can command a price premium over ordinary home machines. Who benefits: Prosumer and enthusiast home buyers who value pro-grade parts; Simonelli, which already sells the Oscar line and can earn a premium on a brand its professional customers recognise.. Why behaviour changes: Buyers who see the commercial components as a signal of quality and durability switch from mid-range appliances to a pro-derived machine, even at a higher price.. How value is captured: Simonelli keeps the price premium through its existing brand and shared component supply, without needing a new consumer distribution system.. Assumptions: Enthusiasts will pay a noticeable premium for commercial-derived components in a home-sized body; Simonelli's brand carries credibility with home buyers, not only with cafés; Existing Oscar-line sales already reach some individual buyers. Predictions: Oscar-line sales or price points will sit above comparable prosumer machines without commercial branding; Buyers in enthusiast forums will cite component quality as the main reason for choosing the model; A price test of a home-sized model with commercial components will hold volume at a premium of about 15-25 percent (estimated, to verify).

T2: Home espresso buyers choose by where and how they can buy, so the value in a consumer proposition sits with whoever controls the consumer channel and brand trust; a manufacturer without that access earns little from a home product and is better placed selling into a strategic acquirer. Who benefits: A consumer-channel owner or strategic acquirer (for example a home-appliance group) that gains a ready prosumer brand; Simonelli would benefit mainly through a sale price rather than organic growth.. Why behaviour changes: Consumers buy where they find trusted retail, service and returns support, so a product without that support loses the sale even if the machine is good.. How value is captured: Value is captured through a sale or licence of a prosumer brand to a company that already runs consumer distribution, rather than by Simonelli building its own retail network.. Assumptions: Consumer channel access, not product quality alone, is the binding constraint on home sales; Acquirers in the prosumer segment pay for brand plus channel; Simonelli would need to build retail and service capability to sell direct to home buyers. Predictions: Prosumer espresso brands that sell through established retail or online channels grow faster than brands that rely on specialist direct sales; Recent deals in the segment price brands on channel reach as well as product; A direct-to-consumer launch without retail partners shows weak sell-through in the first year.

T1 supports, from simo-dcn-oscar-mood-2021 (company_assertion): "the original Nuova Simonelli Oscar, which introduced some of Nuova Simonelli’s high-quality and high-powered components to high-end home and prosumer audiences.". Does not show: This is trade-press reporting of a launch description. It shows the company has sold a home-oriented line with commercial components, not that buyers pay a premium for those components, what volumes sell, or how the price compares with other prosumer machines. Price and sales data were not in the excerpt..

T2 supports, from simo-dcn-breville-lelit-2022 (market_fact): "has announced plans to acquire Italian prosumer espresso equipment company Lelit". Does not show: The article reports a deal and its price. It does not say why Breville bought Lelit, whether it wanted the brand, the product, or consumer channel access, or whether the price reflected channel reach. The claim that channel, not product, drives value is untested here..
Looked for evidence against T1: "home espresso buyers do not pay premium for commercial components price"; found simo-dcn-oscar-mood-2021, simo-slashgear-linea-mini-2015, simo-delonghi-prosumer-2025.

T1 supports, from simo-slashgear-linea-mini-2015 (analogy): "the Linea Mini may still carry an eye-watering price tag but it's potentially a breakthrough in mainstream coffee geekery". Does not show: This is one journalist's 2015 view of a competitor's home machine, with no sales, volume or margin data. It shows a commercial-derived home machine was marketed at a high price, not that enough buyers paid it, and it says nothing about Simonelli's brand. It does not contradict T1, so no contradiction is claimed..

Test "Premium-spec home concept sign-up test with channel split" between T1; T2. Method: Run a paid-deposit pre-order or waitlist landing page for a home-sized machine concept built on commercial-derived components. Show two versions: one that names the commercial components and one with identical specs but generic branding. Also split traffic between a direct sign-up and a sign-up that routes buyers to a partner retailer (partner to be found, not contracted). Recruit traffic through enthusiast forums and paid social in two markets.. Sample: Proposed: about 3,000 unique visitors per arm, roughly 12,000 total, across two markets (estimated); deposits are refundable.. Measure: Conversion to a refundable deposit at each of two price points, and the premium between the commercial-component and generic versions; partner-route conversion versus direct.. Predictions: T1: Commercial-component version converts at a higher rate than generic version at the same price, and the premium holds at the higher price point; channel route makes little difference.; T2: Conversion depends mainly on the retail or partner route being visible and trusted; the component message adds little, and direct-only sign-ups convert far below partner-route sign-ups.. Decision rule: Proposed threshold: keep T1 as lead if the commercial-component version converts at least 15 percent more than generic at the same price, and the premium holds at the higher price point. Move to T2 if the partner-route version converts at least twice the direct-only rate and the component premium is under 5 percent. Otherwise, neither is supported and no product investment is recommended.. Cost: 15000 euros, 8 weeks.

Favours T1: Do not commit to a consumer product investment yet. Run the proposed X1 sign-up test (about 15,000 EUR, 8 weeks, within the 20,000 EUR and 12-week assumed limits) before any design or channel spend. Treat the company's existing Oscar line as the starting evidence, and be clear that the public record shows a home-oriented product exists, not that home buyers pay a premium for it. Beliefs: T1: uncertain; T2: uncertain.

T1 kept: SYN-SIMO-UPDATE is SIMULATED, so it is not evidence and I do not cite it. Read as a what-if, it would point to a mechanism outside T1 and T2: a hands-on learning offer raising reservations with price, brand and warranty held constant. That would need its own theory about skill or ownership experience. It does not show whether component status is true or false, so T1 stays uncertain pending the X1 test. The only real evidence I cite for T1 remains the Oscar launch description. New claim: none. Evidence: simo-dcn-oscar-mood-2021.

T2 kept: SYN-SIMO-UPDATE is SIMULATED and is not evidence, so it does not change T2. Its only relevance is that a skill or ownership offer, not channel reach, moved reservations in the what-if. That is a third mechanism, not a test of channel control. T2 stays uncertain, supported only by the reported Breville-Lelit deal, which does not show why it was made. New claim: none. Evidence: simo-dcn-breville-lelit-2022.

T1 kept: Nothing changed. The only update this stage offered is SIMULATED, so it is excluded and does not move T1. T1 stays uncertain until the X1 test reads out. I also cite the Linea Mini analogy as consistent with, but not proof of, a premium for commercial-derived home machines. New claim: none. Evidence: simo-dcn-oscar-mood-2021; simo-slashgear-linea-mini-2015.

T2 revised: Narrowed. The Breville-Lelit article shows a prosumer brand was bought at about EUR 113 million, but it does not show channel control was the reason. The claim that channel, not product, is the binding constraint is untested and is now stated only as a hypothesis for the X1 partner-route arm. The simulated update is excluded and does not affect this. New claim: Prosumer espresso brands may capture value through consumer channel reach as well as product, as a hypothesis to test in X1 partner-route versus direct sign-up; the mechanism is unconfirmed.. Evidence: simo-dcn-breville-lelit-2022.

T1 kept: Supposing SYN-SIMO-UPDATE were real, it would show a learning-offer effect on reservations with price, brand and warranty held constant. That is a skill or ownership mechanism, not component status, so it would not confirm or reject T1; at most it would call for a new theory. It is SIMULATED, so it changes nothing and is excluded from the evidence for finish. T1 stays uncertain pending X1. New claim: none. Evidence: SYN-SIMO-UPDATE.

Recommendation: Do not commit to a consumer product investment yet. Public sources show Simonelli already sells a home-oriented line (Oscar, with commercial-derived components) and that Breville agreed to buy prosumer maker Lelit for about EUR 113 million. Neither shows home buyers pay a premium for commercial components, or that Simonelli needs its own consumer channel. Run a small test first (proposed X1: about EUR 15,000, 8 weeks, within the assumed limits). Other options stay open until it reads out. Target customer: Enthusiast home espresso buyers who value pro-grade components. Provisional and untested.. Value proposition: A home-sized machine with commercial-derived components, priced above generic prosumer machines. A hypothesis that X1 will test.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run X1: refundable deposit page comparing a commercial-component message with generic branding at two prices, direct versus partner-route sign-up. Keep T1 if the component version converts at least 15 percent more at the same price. Move toward T2 if partner-route conversion is at least twice direct and the premium is under 5 percent. Otherwise recommend no product investment. Also request Oscar unit and price data from the company.. Uncertainty: High. No public data on Oscar volumes, prices, margins or channel mix. The 2021 report is a company claim, in Italian, and does not mention a home product. The Oscar article describes a launch, not demand. Breville-Lelit shows strategic value, not why. Linea Mini (2015) is one journalist's view of a competitor. Simonelli financial data not found publicly. The one SIMULATED result is excluded from all evidence. Searches used: 2 of 8.. Would change if: X1 shows no conversion lift from the component message (premium under 5 percent); Partner-route conversion is at least twice direct, favouring T2; Company data show Oscar units are small or mainly sold to cafés; Public evidence that most home buyers choose on channel or service, not components; A partner offers white-label terms making a consumer launch cheaper. Beliefs: T1: uncertain; T2: uncertain.

After the legal guarantee has expired, the manufacturer is still required to repair common household products, which are technically repairable under EU law, such as washing machines, vacuum cleaners, and even smartphones.

Electrolux Professional provides integrated solutions designed for different formats – laundromats, bungalows and consumer‑operated – combining reliability, resource efficiency and serviceability to maximize uptime and ROI.

events.text: Objective: Decide whether Electrolux Professional Group should invest in a differentiated consumer-facing proposition for a specific laundry or home use case, beyond its professional commercial laundry business, and identify what evidence would justify that investment.. Constraints: Outside analyst using only public sources, with no company contact and no assumed company intentions; Financial and contractual detail may be non-public and must be flagged as not found; Test budget of 20000 EUR and 12-week limit are analyst assumptions, not company figures; Search budget: 7 searches remaining, 1 kept-for-challenge slot; Figures presented as observed must come from sources actually read; proposed figures must be labelled as proposed. Alternatives: No expansion: remain purely professional (B2B commercial laundry and food service) and deprioritise consumers; Product redesign: adapt existing professional machines into a smaller or simpler consumer-grade product for a specific use case; Different route to buyers: sell through existing consumer appliance channels or partner with a consumer brand instead of building an own consumer offer; Different customer group: target adjacent professional-like buyers such as small laundrettes, care homes, hospitality micro-businesses or serviced apartments instead of households; Service or subscription model: offer laundry-as-a-service or rental to individuals or small operators, capturing value through the service rather than hardware; Licensing or white-label: license the professional technology to a consumer brand and take royalty income with low channel risk.
Searched for "Electrolux Professional consumer products households laundry"; found epro-consumer-operated, epro-selfservice-formats, epro-ep-right-to-repair.

T1: EPG's existing consumer reach is indirect: residents of multi-family buildings, students and campsite guests use EPG machines in shared self-service rooms, so a consumer proposition is best built as a placement offer to building owners and operators, not a product sold to households. Who benefits: Building owners, student housing operators and campsite or marina operators who want a revenue-generating or amenity laundry; EPG, which sells machines and service to them.. Why behaviour changes: Owners of shared housing want laundry that works reliably with little staff time, and tenants who lack a home machine will use a coin or card operated room. Owners therefore buy for uptime and return on investment, and tenants accept the existing format.. How value is captured: EPG sells or leases commercial machines and service contracts to the operator, with recurring income from parts, maintenance and consumables; the end user pays the operator, not EPG.. Assumptions: Shared-housing operators buy on uptime and ROI rather than brand; Tenants without a home machine are a large enough group to fill these rooms; EPG's existing self-service range is already sold into these formats. Predictions: Demand growth tracks the number of multi-family and student units without in-unit machines, not household appliance sales; Sales of self-service formats are concentrated in B2B buyers, with little or no direct household sales; Operators' purchase decisions cite uptime, service response and payback rather than consumer features.

T2: Households will pay a premium for a home washing machine that is designed for repair and long life, because EU right-to-repair rules make durability and serviceability a purchase criterion; a maker that owns parts supply and repair can charge for that durability. Who benefits: Households replacing a washing machine who want a machine that lasts and can be fixed; EPG, if it can offer a product plus parts and service at a premium.. Why behaviour changes: EU rules require manufacturers to keep repairing common household products such as washing machines after the legal guarantee expires, which makes repairability and parts availability visible when buyers choose a machine. Buyers who expect a long life are willing to pay more upfront.. How value is captured: A price premium on a durable home machine, plus recurring income from genuine parts, repair visits and extended service plans.. Assumptions: Buyers notice and value repairability at the point of purchase; EPG can build or license a home-scale product that meets the cost ceiling of household appliances; Repair obligations raise the value of a serviceable product relative to a disposable one. Predictions: Premium home machines with published parts availability and longer warranties sell at higher prices than standard models; Buyers who research repairability are more willing to pay for a service plan; Sales growth in repairable models is concentrated in markets with active right-to-repair enforcement.

T1 supports, from epro-consumer-operated (company_assertion): "Consumer‑operated setups enable residents, guests or members to run their own laundry in multi‑family buildings, student housing, campsites, marinas, gyms or staff facilities.". Does not show: It is the company's own product description, not a sales record. It does not show how many units buy these setups, who pays, whether households buy machines for their own homes, or whether operators buy on uptime and payback as T1 predicts..

T2 supports, from epro-ep-right-to-repair (regulation): "After the legal guarantee has expired, the manufacturer is still required to repair common household products, which are technically repairable under EU law, such as washing machines, vacuum cleaners, and even smartphones.". Does not show: It describes a repair obligation in EU law. It does not show that buyers notice repairability when choosing a machine, that they pay a premium for it, or that a durable home machine would earn margin for EPG. It is also a press release summary, not the regulation text..

Looked for evidence against T1: "self-service laundry operators buy on price or tenant demand, not uptime, or household machine ownership makes shared laundry rooms obsolete"; found epro-selfservice-formats, epro-which-no-premium, epro-consumer-operated.

T2 contradicts, from epro-which-no-premium (independent_study): "Our research has found that you don't have to pay a premium to make a sustainable choice. In fact, the cheapest Eco Buy dishwashers and washing machines cost less than £400.". Does not show: This is a UK 2020 consumer-body recommendation about sustainability and price, not about repairability or durability. It does not test whether buyers pay more for a repairable machine, nor whether a parts and service plan earns margin. It shows that eco-rated models were not necessarily priced higher, which weakens the premium assumption of T2 but does not disprove the repair mechanism..

Test "Two-arm demand probe: operator placement interest versus household premium for repairability" between T1; T2. Method: Arm A (T1): semi-structured interviews with operators of shared housing, student housing and campsites, asking about laundry provision, uptime requirements, and willingness to sign a service contract for a machine placed in a shared room. Arm B (T2): an online discrete-choice survey of households replacing a washing machine, with randomised price and a repairability attribute (published parts availability and a longer warranty versus standard).. Sample: Proposed: Arm A, 15 operators across the EU, recruited through trade contacts. Arm B, 400 households in two EU markets with active right-to-repair enforcement, recruited through an online panel. Estimated cost is within budget.. Measure: Arm A: share of operators who state a purchase or contract intention at a stated price and cite uptime or service as the deciding criterion. Arm B: willingness-to-pay premium for the repairable attribute, estimated from the choice model, with its confidence interval.. Predictions: T1: Most operators name uptime, service response and payback as the deciding factors, with at least a third stating a contract intention; households show little or no premium for repairability because the offer is not bought by them.; T2: Households show a positive, statistically distinguishable willingness to pay for the repairable attribute, and operators treat repairability as secondary to price.. Decision rule: Proceed with the operator placement route (T1) if at least 5 of 15 operators (about one third) name uptime or service as the deciding factor and state a contract intention, and the household premium is below 10 per cent. Pursue the household repairability proposition (T2) only if the household premium is at least 10 per cent with a confidence interval excluding zero, and fewer than 5 operators express contract intention. If neither holds, decline further investment in a consumer proposition.. Cost: 14000 euros, 8 weeks.

Favours T1: Do not build a differentiated household consumer proposition yet. The only consumer-facing activity in the public record is placement of self-service laundry in shared housing, operated by residents or guests, which is B2B2C. Test whether building owners and operators will buy a service-backed machine offer before committing to any household product. Keep the household repairability idea (T2) as a secondary hypothesis that the test also checks. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

T1 kept: The simulated warehouse result (SYN-D) measures a label printer and packing errors, so it does not bear on T1 and changes nothing. T1 stands on the company's own description of consumer-operated formats in shared housing, which is a company claim with no sales data. The theory remains a hypothesis to be tested. New claim: none. Evidence: epro-consumer-operated.

T2 revised: The Which? piece found sustainable models were not priced above cheaper ones, which weakens the premium assumption. The EP summary confirms an EU repair obligation but does not show buyers value it or pay for it. The repair mechanism is still possible but the premium claim is unsupported. New claim: EU repair obligations may make parts availability and serviceability a purchase consideration for washing machines, but whether buyers pay a premium for it is unknown and untested.. Evidence: epro-which-no-premium; epro-ep-right-to-repair.

T1 kept: Supposing SYN-D were real, it measures a label printer's effect on packing errors in a warehouse and nothing about shared-housing operators or household buyers, so it would not change T1 at all. It is a simulated result and is not cited as evidence for any claim in this analysis. New claim: none. Evidence: SYN-D.

Recommendation: Do not commit to a differentiated household consumer proposition yet. The only consumer-facing activity in the public record is placement of self-service laundry in shared housing (student housing, multi-family buildings, campsites, marinas), where residents or guests use machines run by an operator. Before funding any household product, test whether operators of shared housing will buy a service-backed machine offer, using the proposed two-arm test (X1) at an estimated 14,000 EUR over 8 weeks. Target customer: Operators of shared housing, student accommodation, campsites and marinas who provide laundry to residents or guests, as the first test segment. Households are a secondary hypothesis.. Value proposition: A reliable, serviceable commercial self-service machine with uptime and service response that operators can buy or lease, with recurring parts and service income for EPG. The household repairability proposition is kept as a secondary hypothesis, not a current recommendation.. Favoured theory: T1. Next action: Run test X1: about 15 operator interviews across the EU and a household discrete-choice survey of about 400 households in two markets with active repair enforcement. Proceed with operators if at least 5 of 15 cite uptime or service and state contract intent, with household premium below 10 per cent.. Uncertainty: Major gaps. No sales, margin or segment data for EPG's self-service or consumer activity was found, and financial and contract detail is not public. The only company source is an undated product page. The sole independent price-premium source is a 2020 UK Which? piece on sustainability, which does not test repairability. Three sources read and three of eight evidence searches used. Budget, sample sizes, thresholds and cost are analyst assumptions or proposals, not observed figures.. Would change if: Disclosed figures show EPG's self-service sales are small or declining; Operators name price or tenant demand, not uptime or service, as the deciding factor; Households show a repairability premium of at least 10 per cent with a confidence interval excluding zero; Shared laundry rooms are replaced by in-unit machines faster than operator placements grow; Evidence that EU repair obligations do not affect household washing machine purchase choice. Beliefs: T1: likely; T2: uncertain.

sources.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. Treat the following only as a what-if. In this hypothetical randomized study, 800 household washing-machine buyers eligible for the same professional-derived washer offer were assigned equally to two descriptions. Both descriptions showed the same machine, brand, price, warranty, availability, service terms and verified specifications. One emphasized durability and repairability; the other emphasized washing performance and the upfront price. No discount or extra service was added. The outcome was a paid, refundable purchase reservation remaining uncancelled after 30 days, counted among all 400 assigned buyers per arm. There were 32 reservations in the durability-and-repairability description arm and 72 in the performance-and-price description arm. This tests the incremental effect of the description in this recruited population, not actual appliance lifetime, delivery capability, market size, profitability or sustained repurchase. A weaker result would not refute a different channel or product theory.
